macro.summary: BREAKING: UnitedHealth ($UNH) surges over +8% after posting stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings.
5-year CDS spreads on Big Tech ($ORCL, $AMZN, $GOOGL, $MSFT) up to ~75bps, near the highest in at least 7 years — investors demanding more credit-risk protection on Big Tech debt.
China's crude oil imports dropped -41% YoY in June, to 29 million tons (~7 million bpd).

Trump said Iran called him and "wants to make a deal"; US stock market extended its rally to a new intraday high on the news. (Contradicted ~13h later by zerohedge reporting continued US strikes on Iran — see below.)
$SPCX has flipped from positive gamma (held since IPO day) to negative gamma as of last Friday — dealer positioning turned less supportive.
Trump told Fox Business's Edward Lawrence: "Oil is going to be a little bit of a yo-yo for a while" — commenting on oil price volatility.

Fed's Cook: the FOMC's hawkish evolution is not really an oil/war story; managing price effects from the AI buildout could be a source of internal disagreement — Fed policy path tied to AI-driven inflation risk, not just energy shocks.

64 consecutive months with US inflation above the Fed's 2% target; quoting Kevin Warsh: "The members of our Committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation" — hawkish Fed narrative building.
Premarket movers: Mag7 mixed (Nvidia -1.5%, others +0.3-1.3%); $ATAI +34% on report Eli Lilly in talks to acquire the psychedelic drugmaker.
Today's retail sales expected to be another strong beat, based on real-time BofA card spending data.
AI-attributed job cuts hit 87,714 in 2026 YTD, per Challenger and Gray — 22% of all 2026 layoffs.
Goldman Sachs: AI agents could drive a 24-fold increase in token consumption by 2030, worsening chip shortages over the next 12-18 months.

$TSM earnings beat (EPS $4.31 vs $3.77 est, revenue $40.2B vs $39.7B est) but stock only -0.22%; UBS says TSMC's surprise capex hike reinforces confidence in the AI supply chain — yet Jim Cramer separately called the muted reaction to "insanely good" numbers a sign the semi market has become "a casino of emotions" since SK Hynix index inclusion.

Unusual options activity: a trader put $300k into $PYPL 50-strike calls (exp 08/07/2026) ahead of news, now up 500%+, as Polymarket odds of Stripe acquiring part of PayPal hit 74% (shareholders reportedly calling the offer too low).

Oil/Iran conflict still escalating: US struck Iran for a 5th straight day and hit a sanctioned oil tanker (just now), which sits in tension with Trump's 22h-old "Iran wants a deal" rally comment. Also: Iraq suspended Basrah oil loadings after a drone attack on a tanker, Ukraine intensified attacks on Russian tankers in the Black Sea, and Russia is sitting on a 135M-barrel crude traffic jam — oil supply-disruption risk stays elevated and headline-driven.

stocks.note: 70% of the top 50 drawdowns over the past 30 days are in the tech sector; the market sold MU and ASML earnings today despite beats — "not an earnings story, still a Fed story." Sector-wide tech-rotation-down call, not a single-name setup.
Only one tech buy since June 17 (a 3% position) attempted a breakout and went from +3% to -8%; author is standing down on adding to the tech sector after the failed test buy.

"$SPCX: Oops..." — 60min chart shows price broke below the IPO price line after rolling over from highs, EMA13 crossed below EMA63 in a declining structure. Bearish breakdown flagged alongside SpotGamma's negative-gamma-flip note on the same name same day.

Not directly tradable yet but a major AI-sector datapoint; note @jimcramer separately said "the market does not have room for Anthropic at this moment... they should wait until fall" — a skeptical counterpoint on timing.

Speculates Apple may be quietly acquiring AI companies to become more self-reliant (vs. leaning on Google/Meta/OpenAI); frames this as a potential AI-capex-hike signal the market isn't pricing in for Apple specifically.
